summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute a 727KB obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook that runs setup.mjs, which downloads the Bun runtime binary (pinned v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, marks it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a single-line 727,680-byte bun-cjs bundle beginning `// @bun @bun-cjs` with a shuffled string-array decoder (WV8StW rotate function, hex-named identifiers, ~1000-entry mixed numeric/string array); it is unreadable, has no source counterpart, and cannot execute under Node — Bun is fetched specifically to run it. The package is named `@hubsync/web-sdk-react` but its package.json description ("Verdocs Web SDK for React"), README, and bundled dist code reference verdocs.com endpoints (api.verdocs.com, beta.verdocs.com, developers.verdocs.com), impersonating the unrelated @verdocs/web-sdk-react SDK. A React SDK has no legitimate need to pull a foreign language runtime at install to execute a large obfuscated blob. This is an alternate-runtime dropper: install-time execution of opaque, likely hostile code delivered through a typosquat/impersonation of a real vendor SDK.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
